title_en: Liu Youxiang v. Luoyang Train Section of Luoyang Railway Branch, Chenzhou Train Service Section of Changsha Railway General Company — dispute over compensation for personal injury or death in railway passenger transport
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over compensation for personal injury or death in railway passenger transport; First instance; Basic People's Court; Henan Province; Hunan Province; Natural person; Legal person; Railway Law; Regulations on Compensation for Damages in Railway Passenger Transport; Regulations on Compulsory Insurance for Accidental Injury of Railway Passengers; Determination of cause of death; Compensation liability of railway transport enterprises; Legality of accident handling procedures; Partially upheld; Death on passenger train; Insufficient evidence of jumping off the train; Cremation of corpse; Accident handling agreement; Dispute over compensation for personal injury or death in passenger transport
full_text_en:
Liu Youxiang v. Luoyang Train Section of Luoyang Railway Sub-administration and Chenzhou Train Depot of Changsha Railway General Company — Dispute over Compensation for Personal Injury in Railway Passenger Transport

Plaintiff: Liu Youxiang, male, a farmer from Luoning County, Henan Province.

Agent ad litem: Liu Xianmin, son of the Plaintiff.

Agent ad litem: Lü Jianguo, lawyer from Tianpai Law Firm, Hengyang City, Hunan Province.

Defendant: Luoyang Train Section of Luoyang Railway Sub-administration.

Representative: Shang Yamin, Director.

Agents ad litem: Ma Jianguo and Wu Zhengquan, cadres of Luoyang Railway Sub-administration.

Defendant: Chenzhou Train Depot of Changsha Railway General Company.

Representative: Chen Anmin, Director.

Agent ad litem: Fan Jiamo, cadre of the Passenger and Freight Transport Office of Chenzhou Train Depot, Changsha Railway General Company.

The Plaintiff, Liu Youxiang, filed a lawsuit with the Hengyang Railway Transport Court of Changsha due to a dispute over compensation for personal injury in railway passenger transport with the Defendants, Luoyang Train Section of Luoyang Railway Sub-administration (hereinafter referred to as Luoyang Train Section) and Chenzhou Train Depot of Changsha Railway General Company (hereinafter referred to as Chenzhou Train Depot).

The Plaintiff alleged: The Plaintiff's son, Liu Fengmin, suddenly died while traveling on Passenger Train No. 522. To date, the two Defendants have been unable to provide valid evidence of the cause of death. The family requested a forensic autopsy, which was refused by the Defendant Chenzhou Train Depot, and they had no choice but to consent to cremation. The two Defendants are responsible for Liu Fengmin's death. The Plaintiff requests the court to order the two Defendants to pay insurance benefits of RMB 20,000, compensation of RMB 40,000, and funeral expenses of RMB 7,000.

The Defendant Luoyang Train Section argued: After the Plaintiff's son, Liu Fengmin, died by jumping off the train, our Section performed its duties in accordance with railway regulations. Liu Fengmin's death was caused by his own actions, and our Section bears no liability according to law. The Defendant Chenzhou Train Depot argued: Our Depot is the unit responsible for handling passenger accident injury cases. Its duties are to investigate the accident, apportion liability, and handle the matter with full authority in the absence of objections. Liu Fengmin's body was handed over to our Depot by the public security personnel after on-site investigation. At the time of handover, the public security department did not raise any request for an autopsy or other matters, so our Depot handled the matter in accordance with the general procedures for handling accidental injury accidents to passengers. Regarding the autopsy request made by the deceased's family, our Depot replied that they should apply to the public security department, which would decide the matter. Thereafter, our Depot received no notice of autopsy from the public security department or any other department. Our Depot reached a consensus with the deceased's family on the aftermath and signed the "Agreement on Investigation and Handling of Accidental Injury Accident to Passenger." The cremation of the body was carried out with the consent of the deceased's family. The entire handling procedure fully complied with the regulations of the Ministry of Railways. According to the materials handed over by Train No. 522 to our Depot, Liu Fengmin's death was caused by his own actions and does not fall within the scope of railway compensation. Therefore, the railway transport enterprise shall not bear compensation liability.

The Hengyang Railway Transport Court of Changsha found upon trial:

On March 7, 1998, Liu Fengmin, son of the Plaintiff Liu Youxiang, and his brother-in-law Yang Baosheng boarded Passenger Train No. 522 (Luoyang to Guangzhou) from Luoyang Station to work in Guangzhou. They sat in seats 90 and 91 of Car No. 7. According to Yang Baosheng, during the journey, Liu Fengmin went to the dining car to eat, while he (Yang Baosheng) was sleeping in his seat. On the evening of the 8th, when the train arrived at Guangzhou Station, he could not find Liu Fengmin. The train staff stated that when the train was running between Chenzhou and Baishidu on the Beijing-Guangzhou Railway, someone reported seeing a passenger jump off the train. They then took statements from two witnesses who claimed to be Li Guizhi and Wang Jiankui, and broadcast a search for the jumper's travel companion, but to no avail. When the train returned to Chenzhou on March 9, the train conductor, train police, and safety officer got off the train at Chenzhou Train Depot and asked Tan Shuyun, the depot's safety officer, whether any passenger had jumped off the train the previous day. Tan said none had been found. The three then returned to Luoyang.

At 7:40 a.m. on March 10, the Baishidu Public Security Station notified Baishidu Station by telephone that a male corpse had been found at kilometer 1944.8 of the Beijing-Guangzhou Railway. At 9:00 a.m. that day, Cao Shunguang, Deputy Stationmaster of Baishidu Station, and Chen Jianhua from the Public Security Station went to the scene, examined and photographed the body, and found on the deceased two tickets for Train No. 522, RMB 50, a telephone directory, and other items. That afternoon, the body and personal effects were handed over to Tan Shuyun of the Defendant Chenzhou Train Depot for handling the aftermath, and the Defendant Luoyang Train Section was notified by telephone. The next morning, the deceased's relatives were notified by telephone according to the entries in the telephone directory. On the 13th, three relatives, including the Plaintiff Liu Youxiang, arrived at Chenzhou Train Depot. After confirming that the deceased was Liu Fengmin, they requested a forensic autopsy. Tan Shuyun stated that the Depot could not and did not have the authority to perform such an autopsy. On March 20, Liu Fengmin's body was cremated, and Chenzhou Train Depot advanced funeral expenses of RMB 1,600. On March 21, Tan Shuyun, as the representative of the Accident Handling Committee of Chenzhou Train Depot, relying on the statements of Li Guizhi and Wang Jiankui, handed over by Train No. 522, regarding the discovery of someone jumping off the train, concluded that Liu Fengmin's death was caused by his own reasons. He signed the "Agreement on Investigation and Handling of Accidental Injury Accident to Passenger" with the deceased's elder brother, Liu Xianmin, and paid a one-time insurance benefit of RMB 3,500 to Liu Youxiang. After returning home, Liu Youxiang went to look for the witnesses based on the names and addresses provided by Chenzhou Train Depot. He found that one address did not exist and the other person did not exist by that name. Liu Youxiang believed that Liu Fengmin did not die from jumping off the train and that the two Defendants were responsible for Liu Fengmin's death, so he filed this lawsuit.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the deceased Liu Fengmin's train tickets, passenger transport records, records of passenger injury and death accidents, certificates from Yangzhuang Village Committee of Yangzhuang Town, Baofeng County, Henan Province, confirming that no person named Li Guizhi exists in that village, and certificates from Ruzhou Town, Ruzhou City, Henan Province, confirming that no Tangwang Village or person named Wang Jiankui exists in that town, as well as the court hearing records, which are sufficient for determination.

The Hengyang Railway Transport Court of Changsha held:

Article 58, paragraph 1 of the "Railway Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "If personal injury or death is caused by a railway traffic accident or other railway operation accident, the railway transport enterprise shall bear compensation liability; if the personal injury or death is caused by force majeure or by the victim's own reasons, the railway transport enterprise shall not bear compensation liability." The evidence provided by the Plaintiff Liu Youxiang shows that based on the addresses and names provided by the witnesses, no matching persons could be found. The Defendant Luoyang Train Section relied on the statements of witnesses Li Guizhi and Wang Jiankui to determine that Liu Fengmin died by "jumping off the train himself." Since the whereabouts of these two witnesses are unknown, this evidence does not have legal force and shall not be admitted. Based on the currently available information, the claim that Liu Fengmin died by "jumping off the train himself" cannot be established; it can only be inferred that he died from falling off the train. Since Luoyang Train Section cannot effectively prove that Liu Fengmin's death was due to his own reasons, it shall bear compensation liability in accordance with Article 58, paragraph 1 of the Railway Law. Pursuant to Article 5 of the "Regulations on Compensation for Damages in Railway Passenger Transport" (hereinafter referred to as the Compensation Regulations), approved by the State Council with Document Guo Han (1994) No. 81 and promulgated by the Ministry of Railways on August 13, 1994, and Article 18 of the "Measures for Handling Personal Injury to Railway Passengers and Loss of Luggage," the railway transport enterprise shall compensate Liu Youxiang up to the maximum limit of RMB 40,000 for which the railway bears compensation liability. Article 6 of the Compensation Regulations further provides: "The payment of compensation by the railway transport enterprise in accordance with these Regulations shall not affect the passenger's right to receive insurance benefits in accordance with the state's regulations on compulsory accident insurance for railway passengers." Therefore, while claiming compensation, Liu Youxiang also has the right to request payment of insurance benefits. Article 5 of the "Regulations on Compulsory Accident Insurance for Railway Passengers," as amended on June 5, 1992, provides: "The insured amount for passengers, regardless of seat class, full ticket, half ticket, or free ticket, shall be uniformly set at RMB 20,000 per person." Article 8, item (a) provides: "In case of death, the full insured amount shall be paid." Luoyang Train Section shall also pay insurance benefits of RMB 20,000 to Liu Youxiang in accordance with this provision.

Article 14 of the "Measures for Handling Personal Injury to Railway Passengers and Loss of Luggage," promulgated by the Ministry of Railways with Document Tie Yun (1995) No. 52, provides: "In the event of a passenger injury accident, an accident handling committee shall be established. The accident handling committee shall be composed of the accident handling station (train depot), the relevant section of the accident, the station public security police station, and the passenger or their family members or agents (not exceeding two persons). The stationmaster (depot chief) of the handling station (train depot) shall serve as the chairman. When necessary, the sub-administration director shall serve as the chairman." After Liu Fengmin's death, the Defendant Chenzhou Train Depot, in violation of the above provision, formed an accident handling committee without the participation of public security authorities and signed the "Agreement on Investigation and Handling of Accidental Injury Accident to Passenger" with the deceased's relatives. The signed agreement shall be deemed invalid. Chenzhou Train Depot shall bear responsibility for improper handling of the accident.

Article 4, paragraph (3) of the "Procedures for Handling Compulsory Accident Insurance for Railway Passengers" provides: "If the railway arranges for the coffin and burial of the passenger, the expenses shall be deducted by the insurance company or its agency from the insured amount paid to that passenger." Liu Fengmin's body was cremated by Chenzhou Train Depot on behalf of the family, with the consent of his family members. The Plaintiff Liu Youxiang's claim for compensation of RMB 7,000 for funeral expenses from the two Defendants is not supported.

Accordingly, on July 24, 1998, the Hengyang Railway Transport Court of Changsha entered the following judgment:

1. The Defendant Luoyang Train Section shall pay the Plaintiff Liu Youxiang compensation of RMB 34,900 and insurance benefits of RMB 20,000.

2. The Defendant Chenzhou Train Depot shall pay the Plaintiff Liu Youxiang compensation of RMB 5,100. Court costs for this case of RMB 2,520 shall be borne by the Defendant Luoyang Train Section in the amount of RMB 2,305 and by the Defendant Chenzhou Train Depot in the amount of RMB 215.

The total amount of items 1 and 2 above plus court costs amounts to RMB 62,520. After deducting the insurance benefits of RMB 3,500 already paid by Chenzhou Train Depot to the Plaintiff and the advanced funeral expenses of RMB 1,600, the remaining balance shall be paid within 10 days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective.

The Defendant Luoyang Train Section, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Guangzhou Railway Transport Intermediate Court. The grounds for appeal were: 1. According to railway passenger transport regulations, our Section should not be the defendant in this case; the accident handling station should be the respondent. 2. The first-instance court's conclusion that Liu Fengmin's death was not caused by his own reasons, based solely on the inability to verify the identities of the two witnesses, is improper; the train did not violate railway regulations, and the train staff's handling at the time was appropriate; our Section should not bear compensation liability; the amount of compensation our Section should bear must be determined by the accident handling committee, not by the court. 3. The insurance benefits should be paid by the accident handling station, not by our Section. Therefore, the appeal requested the reversal of the first-instance judgment.

The Appellee Liu Youxiang argued in response that the first-instance court's judgment was correct and should be affirmed.

Upon trial, the Guangzhou Railway Transport Intermediate Court held:

The Plaintiff Liu Youxiang's son, Liu Fengmin, died while traveling on Train No. 522. The Appellant Luoyang Train Section is both the entity responsible for this railway passenger death accident and the subject of the lawsuit named in the Plaintiff's complaint. It was not improper for the first-instance court to list it as a defendant in this case. The Appellant's ground of appeal that it should not be the defendant in this case cannot be established.

Pursuant to Article 58 of the Railway Law, the Appellant Luoyang Train Section, as the direct carrier, must bear the burden of proof if it disagrees with Liu Youxiang's claim. Although the Section submitted evidentiary materials from two passengers and staff members of Train No. 522, because the identities of the two passengers cannot be confirmed, and the train staff are interested parties, these statements do not have legal force. Luoyang Train Section cannot submit valid evidence that Liu Fengmin's death was caused by his own reasons and shall bear compensation liability in accordance with the law. The first-instance court's determination that the statements of the two passengers have no legal force is correct. The Appellant's ground of appeal that this determination is improper cannot be sustained.

Once this dispute was brought to court by the Plaintiff and entered judicial proceedings, upon examination it fell within the jurisdiction of the court and should be tried by the court in accordance with the law. The Appellant Luoyang Train Section's ground of appeal that, after the dispute entered litigation, the internal railway procedures for handling accidents should apply, and that the matter should be adjudicated by an accident investigation and handling committee, cannot be accepted.

According to Article 3, item 5 of the "Regulations on Specific Work after the Railway Takes Over Compulsory Accident Insurance for Railway Passengers," promulgated by the Ministry of Railways, in the event of a passenger's death, the insurance benefits shall in principle be paid by the station near the place where the accident occurred. After Liu Fengmin's death, the insurance benefits should be paid by the accident handling station, i.e., the Appellee Chenzhou Train Depot. The first-instance judgment's order that the Appellant Luoyang Train Section pay such benefits is improper. This ground of appeal by Luoyang Train Section is well-founded and shall be supported.

The accident investigation and handling committee formed by the Appellee Chenzhou Train Depot violated Article 14 of the "Measures for Handling Personal Injury to Railway Passengers and Loss of Luggage" by signing the "Agreement on Investigation and Handling of Accidental Injury Accident to Passenger" with the Appellee Liu Youxiang without the participation of public security authorities. This only indicates that Chenzhou Train Depot improperly handled the accident, but Chenzhou Train Depot bears no liability for Liu Fengmin's death from falling off the train. The first-instance court's decision to order it to bear part of the compensation liability due to improper handling of the accident is incorrect and shall be corrected.

In summary, among the grounds of appeal of the Appellant Luoyang Train Section, only the ground that Chenzhou Train Depot should pay the insurance benefits is well-founded; the rest shall not be adopted. The facts found in the first-instance judgment were clear, and the evidence was reliable and sufficient, but the application of law was improper in certain aspects. The Guangzhou Railway Transport Intermediate Court, in accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, entered the following judgment on October 26, 1998:

1. Item 1 of the first-instance judgment is modified to: The Appellant Luoyang Train Section shall pay the Appellee Liu Youxiang compensation of RMB 40,000.

2. Item 2 of the first-instance judgment is modified to: The Appellee Chenzhou Train Depot shall pay the Appellee Liu Youxiang insurance benefits of RMB 20,000 (the insurance benefits of RMB 3,500 already paid and the advanced funeral expenses of RMB 1,600 shall be offset against this amount). Court costs for the first instance of RMB 2,520 shall be borne by Luoyang Train Section in the amount of RMB 2,016 and by Chenzhou Train Depot in the amount of RMB 504; court costs for the second instance of RMB 2,520 shall be borne by Luoyang Train Section in the amount of RMB 2,016 and by Chenzhou Train Depot in the amount of RMB 504.
